references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew: Jesus says that from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven has been advancing with force, and those who take it by force seize it. He adds that all the prophets and the Law prophesied until John. This is the closest parallel to [ref:Luk 16:16|Luke 16:16], with the same theme about the Law and the prophets up to John, and that God's kingdom breaks forth with power.

Jesus says that among those born of women, no one has arisen greater than John the Baptist, yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than him ([ref:Matt 11:11|Matthew 11:11]). This underscores John's role as a turning point between the old and the new covenant.

John the Baptist began to preach: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near!" ([ref:Matt 3:1-2|Matthew 3:1-2]). This shows that the preaching of God's kingdom began with John, as Jesus points out in [ref:Luk 16:16|Luke 16:16].

Jesus says he has not come to abolish the Law or the Prophets but to fulfill them ([ref:Matt 5:17|Matthew 5:17]). This connects with the fact that the Law and the Prophets were in effect until John, after which God's kingdom is preached – without thereby abolishing the Law (cf. [ref:Luk 16:17|Luke 16:17]).

The next verse ([ref:Luk 16:17|Luke 16:17]) emphasizes that even though God's kingdom is now being preached, it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one tiny stroke of the Law to fall away. The Law thus does not lose its validity.

Paul speaks of John preaching a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel, and that John pointed forward to the one who was coming after him ([ref:Apg 13:24-25|Acts 13:24-25]). John marks the transition from the time of the Law and the Prophets to the time of the gospel.

Paul writes that Christ is the end (goal) of the Law for righteousness to everyone who believes ([ref:Rom 10:4|Romans 10:4]). This illuminates how the Law and the Prophets pointed forward to Christ, and from John's time onward God's kingdom is preached.

Jesus says that among those born of women no one is greater than John, and the people and the tax collectors gave God justice when they were baptized with John's baptism ([ref:Luk 7:28-29|Luke 7:28-29]). Everyone pressed in – even tax collectors – which reflects that "everyone presses in" to God's kingdom.

The risen Jesus, starting from Moses and all the Prophets, explained to them what was written about him in all the Scriptures ([ref:Luk 24:27|Luke 24:27]). The Law and the Prophets all pointed forward to Christ and God's kingdom.

The prophet Isaiah foretold that the Lord's Spirit was upon the anointed one to preach good news to the poor ([ref:Jes 61:1-2|Isaiah 61:1-2]). Jesus quotes this in [ref:Luk 4:18-19|Luke 4:18-19] as the fulfillment of the prophecies – the gospel of God's kingdom now being preached.
